## Summary

Infinix was founded in April 2013 by Transsion and is part of Transsion Holdings, with a registered office in the New Territories, Hong Kong and operational headquarters in Shenzhen; it sells ZERO, NOTE, HOT, S, SMART and GT series phones and Inbook, Zerobook and GT Book laptops, and its XOS operating system is closed source [1]. Transsion runs the TECNO, itel and Infinix brands and sells in Africa, West, South and Southeast Asia and South America [3]. The IEEE registry lists 38 MA-L blocks to "Infinix mobility limited" at a Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong address [2].

A MAC in an Infinix block is most likely an Infinix phone or laptop [1][2]. Upstream's Secure-D, which found Triada and xHelper preinstalled on TECNO W2 phones in 2020, reported no signs of the malware on other Transsion models including Infinix [4], so security notes are empty. Radios, silicon and randomization are unknown: Infinix's site gave no product specifications to the session that wrote this entry [5], no Infinix teardown or specification page was reachable, and the FCC ID databases refused automated access; nothing is filled in from memory.
